slot.brief: Capacitor network with some series and parallel elements; redraw the circuit and find the equivalent capacitance between two terminals; circuit figure required.

stem: For the capacitor network shown, the equivalent capacitance between terminals $A$ and $B$ is:

verdicts.working: The two 4 μF capacitors are in series, giving 2 μF. This branch is in parallel with the 3 μF capacitor, so C_eq = 2 + 3 = 5 μF.

working:

Independent check: The two 4 μF capacitors are in series, giving 2 μF. This branch is in parallel with the 3 μF capacitor, so C_eq = 2 + 3 = 5 μF.
solution:
The two $4\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitors are in series, so
$$C_s=\frac{4\times4}{4+4}=2\,\mu\text{F}.$$
This branch is in parallel with the $3\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor; hence $C_{AB}=2+3=5\,\mu\text{F}$. The answer is (D).

figure.description: Draw two terminals labelled A and B, one at the left and one at the right. Connect A to B with two parallel paths. In the upper path, place two capacitor symbols in series, each labelled 4 μF, with a junction between them. In the lower path, place one capacitor symbol labelled 3 μF. Show wires connecting both ends of each path to the respective A and B terminals. No battery or other components.

draft.distractor_notes: A: Treats all three capacitors as being in series. B: Omits the parallel branch. D: Adds all three capacitances as if they were in parallel.
